successCriteria.description: The LeaveBalance model interface is defined with the exact specified fields (id, employeeId, leavePolicyId, totalEntitlement, usedDays, fiscalYear, status union of ACTIVE|EXHAUSTED|CLOSED, createdAt, updatedAt) and does NOT declare a stored remainingDays field.

The ILeaveBalanceRepository interface declares all four methods with the specified signatures: findByEmployeeAndPolicy returns Promise<LeaveBalance | null>, findByEmployee returns Promise<LeaveBalance[]>, create accepts Omit<LeaveBalance,'id'|'createdAt'|'updatedAt'> and returns Promise<LeaveBalance>, updateUsedDays returns Promise<LeaveBalance>.

The LeaveBalanceRepository class implements ILeaveBalanceRepository using the shared pg Pool and computes remainingDays as totalEntitlement - usedDays, attaching it as a derived property on every object returned by its read methods (findByEmployeeAndPolicy and findByEmployee).

The ILeaveBalanceService interface declares getBalance returning Promise<LeaveBalance & { remainingDays: number }>, deductDays returning Promise<void>, and restoreDays returning Promise<void>, with the specified parameter lists.

The module barrel (index.ts) re-exports the LeaveBalance model, the ILeaveBalanceRepository interface and LeaveBalanceRepository class, and the ILeaveBalanceService interface — matching the leave-policy barrel's export surface shape.

Repository unit tests in tests/unit/modules/leave-balance/leave-balance.repository.test.ts cover, for each repository method: a happy-path return, a null/empty-path return, a parameterized-query assertion (SQL-injection string passed as a parameter value, not interpolated), and an error path that rejects with a 'Failed to …: <message>' error.

The create method persists a new leave_balances row from the Omit input (employeeId, leavePolicyId, totalEntitlement, usedDays, fiscalYear, status) and returns the created LeaveBalance with generated id/createdAt/updatedAt plus the derived remainingDays property.
The updateUsedDays method updates the used_days column for a given balance id and returns the updated LeaveBalance carrying the recomputed derived remainingDays property.

constraints: remainingDays must never be a stored column or a writable field; it is always computed at query time as totalEntitlement - usedDays and attached as a derived property on returned objects. No code path writes remainingDays to the database.

All database access must go through the repository layer (GP-001); the repository must use the shared pg Pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts and parameterized SQL ($1, $2, …) — never string-interpolated values.

Every repository method must wrap its DB call in try/catch and throw new Error('Failed to <action>: <message>') where message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error), matching the employee and leave-policy repository error convention.
Strict TypeScript must pass (tsc --noEmit): no implicit any, strict null checks. Use unknown with type guards instead of any (HARNESS no-any rule).
The service interface file must be interface-only (method signatures only, no implementation), importing the LeaveBalance model — matching the leave-policy service-interface convention.

Modules must import from each other only through their declared public entry point (index.ts); no circular dependencies. The leave-balance module depends on leave-policy and employee models only as type references, not as runtime imports of their internals.

Test files must use the project Jest convention (*.test.ts under tests/, matching testMatch), mock pg via jest.mock('pg') with a shared jest.fn() query, use snake_case mock rows, and follow the established beforeEach/clearAllMocks/instantiate-with-mock-pool pattern from the employee and leave-policy repository tests.

fiscalYear equals the calendar year (Jan 1–Dec 31); used_days is the denormalized source of truth (deduct-on-submission, restore-on-reject/cancel). This phase only defines the model/repository/service-interface — it does not implement the deduction/restore business logic (that is Phase 10).
outOfScope: LeaveBalanceService implementation (the class that implements ILeaveBalanceService with deductDays/restoreDays business logic, balance-sufficiency checks, and floor-at-zero) — deferred to Phase 10.
LeaveBalance controller and Fastify routes — not part of this phase; no HTTP surface is built here.
Database migrations / DDL for the leave_balances table — this phase defines the TypeScript model and repository against the conceptual schema; migration creation is out of scope.

Audit logging (GP-002) integration for balance mutations — the repository's create/updateUsedDays are data-access operations; audit recording is wired in later phases, not in this model/repository/service-interface phase.

Balance-sufficiency enforcement (BR-BALANCE-SUFFICIENCY: remainingDays >= requested days) and the deduct-on-submission / restore-on-reject business rules — these belong to the service implementation (Phase 10) and the LeaveRequest orchestrator (Phase 7), not this interface-definition phase.
Service-interface unit tests — only the repository unit test file is specified for this phase; service tests come with the service implementation in Phase 10.

entityInvariants.invariant: A LeaveBalance is uniquely identified by the composite (employeeId, leavePolicyId, fiscalYear); at most one balance row exists per employee/policy/year. The repository's findByEmployeeAndPolicy lookup keys on this composite.

remainingDays is a derived, non-stored value equal to totalEntitlement - usedDays, computed at query time and present as a property on every object returned by repository read methods; it is never persisted and never written by any code path.

The status lifecycle is ACTIVE → EXHAUSTED → CLOSED; status is one of the three literal union values. A balance whose usedDays reaches totalEntitlement is EXHAUSTED; CLOSED is a terminal state. (Status transitions are enforced by the service in a later phase; this phase only models the union.)

usedDays is the denormalized source of truth for consumed leave and is the only mutable consumption field; it is incremented on submission and decremented on reject/cancel by the service layer. The repository exposes updateUsedDays as the single mutation primitive for consumption.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the matching LeaveBalance (with derived remainingDays) or null when no row matches the composite key; throws Error('Failed to …: <msg>') on DB failure.
Returns all LeaveBalance rows for the employee in the given fiscal year (each carrying derived remainingDays), or an empty array when none exist; throws Error('Failed to …: <msg>') on DB failure.

Persists a new leave_balances row from the provided employeeId, leavePolicyId, totalEntitlement, usedDays, fiscalYear, status and returns the created LeaveBalance with generated id/createdAt/updatedAt plus derived remainingDays; throws Error('Failed to …: <msg>') on DB failure (including unique-constraint violation on the composite key).
Updates the used_days column for the given balance id and returns the updated LeaveBalance with recomputed derived remainingDays; throws Error('Failed to …: <msg>') on DB failure.
Returns the balance augmented with remainingDays (LeaveBalance & { remainingDays: number }); behavior on missing balance is defined by the service implementation in a later phase.
Resolves void on success; the implementation (Phase 10) must reject when the deduction would drive remaining below zero. This phase only declares the signature.
Resolves void on success; the implementation (Phase 10) must floor usedDays at zero. This phase only declares the signature.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The LeaveBalanceRepository must follow the same structural conventions as the leave-policy repository: import { Pool, QueryResult } from 'pg' and { pool } from '../../shared/db/connection'; a module-level rowTo<Entity> helper mapping snake_case DB columns to camelCase model fields (with ?? null / ?? undefined for nullable columns); a class with private readonly db: Pool and constructor(dbPool: Pool = pool); try/catch in every method throwing 'Failed to <action>: <message>'; parameterized SQL via $1/$2; SELECT * pattern; empty rows return null/[].

The leave-balance service interface file must be interface-only (signatures only, no implementation), importing the LeaveBalance model, matching the leave-policy service-interface file's shape and export style.
The leave-balance barrel (index.ts) must re-export the model, the repository interface and class, and the service interface, matching the leave-policy barrel's export surface and ordering convention.

The leave-balance repository test must mirror the leave-policy repository test structure: jest.mock('pg') returning a Pool whose query is a shared jest.fn(); snake_case mock rows typed Record<string, unknown>; an expect<Entity>MatchesRow helper; beforeEach clearing mocks, creating a mocked Pool, extracting mockQuery, and instantiating the repo with the mock pool; each method tested for happy path, null/empty path, parameterized-query (SQL-injection) assertion, and error path rejecting with 'Failed to …: <msg>'.

The LeaveBalance model and repository must align with the reconciled architecture's leave_balances conceptual schema (id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at; unique composite on employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year) with the binding deviation that remaining_days is NOT stored — it is computed as totalEntitlement - usedDays at query time per the settled business rules.

The leave-balance module's employeeId field must reference the Employee entity's id (string) as defined in the employee model; the repository's employeeId parameter and the leave_balances.employee_id FK conceptually target employees.id.

The leave-balance module's leavePolicyId field must reference the LeavePolicy entity's id (string) as defined in the leave-policy model; the repository's leavePolicyId parameter and the leave_balances.leave_policy_id FK conceptually target leave_policies.id.

integrationPoints.why: The LeaveBalanceRepository must obtain its pg Pool from the shared database connection (the exported `pool`), as the default constructor argument, matching the employee and leave-policy repositories.

The LeaveBalance.leavePolicyId references a LeavePolicy by id; the leave-balance module depends on the leave-policy model (Phase 4) as a type/FK reference per the reconciled dependency map (leave-balance → leave-policy).
The LeaveBalance.employeeId references an Employee by id; the leave-balance module depends on the employee model (Phase 2) as a type/FK reference per the reconciled dependency map.

The ILeaveBalanceService interface declared in this phase is consumed by the LeaveRequest orchestrator in Phase 7 for balance lookup, deduction on submission, and restoration on reject/cancel; this phase establishes the contract that later phases implement and consume.

The ILeaveBalanceService interface declared here is implemented in Phase 10 (LeaveBalanceService with deductDays/restoreDays business logic, balance-sufficiency checks, floor-at-zero); this phase defines the interface the implementation must satisfy.
